evals.prompt: Chart the 11 random numbers as a bar chart in Vega-Lite.
evals.expected_output: A plan that puts a Python node between the node that returns the list of numbers and a new Vega-Lite node, turning the list into a DataFrame, since a Vega-Lite node takes only a DataFrame or a GeoDataFrame.
assertions: The answer writes a dataflow plan (dataflow.plan.write).

The plan does not feed the list itself into the Vega-Lite node: a Python node it adds turns the list from node 7877e099-7c1b-4496-8be7-43264794aea4 into a DataFrame first, or the answer also changes that node so it returns a DataFrame.
The Vega-Lite node receives exactly one data edge, from the node that hands it the table.

evals.prompt: Save the top 10 zip codes to a CSV file with a Data Export node, then draw a second bar chart from the exported file.
evals.expected_output: A plan with a Data Export node fed by the top 10 node and a new Vega-Lite chart fed by that same top 10 node, since a Data Export node has no output: no edge leaves the Data Export node.
assertions: The answer writes a dataflow plan (dataflow.plan.write).
The plan adds a Data Export node (curio.builtin/data-export) fed by the top 10 node, f9e2b9af-23e6-4db3-9140-38bfecd6afc5.
No data edge in the plan leaves the Data Export node.
The second chart's data edge comes from f9e2b9af-23e6-4db3-9140-38bfecd6afc5, the table the export writes, not from the Data Export node.

evals.prompt: Plan a dataflow that loads the SCOUT flood depth raster for 2050 to 2080 without NbS from my Data Catalog and shows its depths as a Vega-Lite heatmap.
evals.expected_output: A plan in which a Python node turns the raster's cells into a table of positions and depths before the Vega-Lite heatmap, since a Vega-Lite node takes only a DataFrame or a GeoDataFrame; no edge carries the raster itself into the chart.
assertions: The answer writes a dataflow plan (dataflow.plan.write).

No data edge carries the raster itself into the Vega-Lite node: the node that feeds the chart hands it a table (a DataFrame) of cell positions and depths, made from the raster by Python code, in a node of its own or in a loader whose intent says it turns the cells into such a table.
The Vega-Lite node receives exactly one data edge.
